newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY TO RAISE FUEL PRICES AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY TO RAISE FUEL PRICES AUG 11.

text.p: Poland's second biggest Gdansk refinery said in a Friday statement it would raise its fuel and diesel prices by 30 zlotys per tonne as of August 11 due to rising world oil prices and a weaker zloty.
The rise will be the refinery's second in two weeks after the it raised its prices by 20 zlotys per tonne on Wednesday.

"The fuel price rise by the Gdansk refinery is a result of increased costs of buying crude oil, higher costs of importing fuel and, most of all, the dollar/zloty exchange rate," the refinery's spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka said.
She said the Wednesday fuel price rise increased retail fuel prices at filling stations by about 0.03 zlotys per litre.
"What retail price rises will follow after this price increase is up to the owners of the petrol stations," she said.

Poland's biggest refinery, Petrochemia Plock, also raised its prices earlier this week and a source at Petrochemia said the refinery might further increase its petrol price because of the higher crude price and the weaker zloty.
